newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam bank sued in payment row over $500,000 LC.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam bank sued in payment row over $500,000 LC.

text.p: Executives at a leading Vietnamese state-owned bank said on Monday they were examining their legal options following a court decision in Singapore to freeze their local assets amid a row over payment on a $500,000 Letter of Credit.

Officials at the Industrial and Commercial Bank of Vietnam (Vietincombank) told Reuters that Mees Pierson N.V. (Singapore branch) had obtained court injunctions freezing the Nostro accounts of Vietincombank held in Singapore banks.
A first ruling, on June 26, was against Vietincombank's Binh Thuan branch. A subsequent ruling on July 3 saw the injunction widened to cover the assets of Vietincombank and all its branches.
Details of the amounts involved were not available but one executive put the value of those assets at around $100,000.

The dispute between Mees Pierson and Vietincombank centres around a letter of credit issued in December 1995 to the Binh Thuan Production Import-Export and Trading Company for the import of flour worth $500,000 from Bay Pacific PTE Ltd.
Vietincombank said in a statement the shipment had not arrived and the Binh Thuan company had therefore been unable to pay.

It said the terms of the LC stipulated that Standard Chartered Bank (Singapore Branch) was authorised to act as the advising negotiating and confirming bank, but this role had been assumed by Mees Pierson without Vietincombank having been informed.
"Therefore Vietincombank (Binh Thuan Branch) has the full right to refuse making payment for the said LC documents... ," it said.

"By suing Vietincombank (Binh Thuan Branch) at the High Court of Singapore and by self-deciding to block Vietincombank's (Binh Thuan Branch) Nostro accounts maintained with banks in Singapore, Meespierson N.V. (Singapore) and the High Court of Singapore have damaged the reputation of our bank."
Executives at Mees Pierson said the company had no comment at the present time. Court officials in Singapore said a further summons in chambers had been scheduled for August 8.
The problem comes at a critical juncture for Vietnam's domestic banking industry, which is already reeling from a wider loans crisis surrounding Letter of Credit and other debt repayments.
The collapse into scandal in March of leading conglomerates Minh Phung and Epco has left several banks facing potentially huge losses as a result of loosely managed chain loans made to the two firms.

In one twist to the problems a Vietnamese banker caught up in the scandal was found dead in May inside Vietincombank's Ho Chi Minh City headquarters. His body was found in a lift room with his face against an electrical circuit board.
Vietnam's state media reported on Monday that the authorities had classified the case as suicide.
